title: The ACE asset and data-product read of the trace has no grant to S4, no published operation and no contract row in the plan
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-017, its Acceptance criteria AC2, Data table row v_ace_npa_asset DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219, Endpoints and Data rows rule_row and decision_log_entry); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.17.2 integration points NCB and Model gateway, A2.17.3.1 VR-S4-017-1, A2.17.3.3, Requirements served); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T3.1, T3.3, T5.2, T5.3, appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (row FEAT-LIT-17); _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4: two tables hearing and legal_action, five REST operations, zero events, zero jobs, one workflow); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (C list of both slices, empty)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 4 and 6; s8 BR3; s11 Data; s12.2; s12.7; s12.8; s13 Solution plan; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s3, s7 AC3 and AC5, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.7, s12.8, s19
description: The legacy step reads the debtor's assets from the ACE view v_ace_npa_asset and judges the freshness of that data product from v_ace_batch_status (VR-S4-017-1), and both slices of RWB-E5-017 therefore need that read. In the target no source gives S4 the read. The architecture keeps the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views read only by rwb-source-data, DP-05 allows either the owner's contract or the service's own ACE view, and the context pack gives S4 two tables, hearing and legal_action, and no view. The FSD S4 A2.17.2 names NCB and the Model gateway as its integration points and no data product read, TSD S4 T5.2 names the published Java interfaces P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 with no operation, T-A.1 lists five S4 operations only, and the contract-dependency row of both slices is None. The operation name of the read and the field names of the batch status are therefore Not specified in the source documents, and both stories declare the read as a consumed contract of rwb-source-data answered by a fake, with no v_ace_* grant and no ACE table statement anywhere in the build.
evidence: Legacy Data table row: v_ace_npa_asset, asset_ref, asset_key, asset_code, transfer_in_type, from_segment, book_value and 6 more, DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219. FSD S4 A2.17.2 Integration points: NCB, Model gateway. FSD S4 A2.17.3.1 VR-S4-017-1: Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (v_ace_batch_status) with MSG-P1-001. Context pack ownership rows of S4: tables hearing and legal_action, REST operations five, events none, jobs none. TSD S4 T5.2 lists the published Java interfaces P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 with no operation name. T-A.1 lists API-S4-001 to API-S4-005 only. split_plan C list for RWB-S4-E5017-APP and RWB-S4-E5017-CON is empty.
area: Data access and service contracts, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner
proposed: Publish the asset and batch-status read on rwb-source-data's contract with its fake, add the class C row RWB-P1-E5017-C to both slices in step D1, and record the refused v_ace_* grant in the Service Contract Catalog so no later build asks S4 for a view.

description: R-LIT-50 traces assets across NCB, internal data, registries and insurers, and the FSD names NCB and the Model gateway as the integration points of the feature; FEAT-AGT-01, the prerequisite of the legacy story, is the agent that decides what to search. No source turns either into a contract of this service. The legacy story's dependency list and the plan carry no contract, integration or external dependency row for RWB-E5-017, S4 owns no adapter, no file and no external system row in its ownership rows, TSD S4 T5.1 gives the module only INT-09 (LIT, inbound, COLLINS batch) and INT-33 (Legal Execution Department and courts, as entered through the law firms), and neither the FSD nor the TSD names an operation for the bureau, the registries, the insurers or the trace plan. The search is therefore a consumed contract of rwb-integration (P2), one call per source with the 2 s one-hop rule, the trace plan a consumed contract of rwb-agent (P10), and both are faked; the operation names are Not specified in the source documents.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.17.2 Integration points: NCB, Model gateway. FSD S4 A1.1 Dependencies: FEAT-AGT-01, FEAT-APD-01, FEAT-CWC-11, FEAT-DCM-02, FEAT-DRI-14, FEAT-DRI-17, FEAT-LIT-04, FEAT-DCM-16, FEAT-LIT-05. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-50 systems column: NCB, registries, insurers; R-LIT-52 systems column: Workbench. TSD S4 T5.1: INT-09 LIT in, COLLINS batch, daily end of day; INT-33 Legal Execution Department and courts, in, through the law firms, as entered. Context pack: no adapter, no external row, no event, no job; DP-05 and DP-20 outside the planned model. split_plan C, I and X lists of both slices are empty.

title: The trigger of the trace step is not stated by any source and no event, subscription or Schedule is declared for it
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-017, Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC2, permission table); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.17.2 step 1, A2.17.3.3 roles, A2.17.4.4 system background events); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T2, T5.3, T-A.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-LIT-44, R-LIT-50, R-LIT-52); _work/msr/context/S4.md (events none, jobs none, workflows one, queue rwb-litigation)
section: APP s4 Flow step 1; s8 BR7; s9 State transitions; s10 Authority; s12.3; s12.4; s12.5; s12.6; CON s7 AC4, s12.3, s12.4, s12.5, s12.6
description: The legacy criterion opens with Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place and When its trigger arrives, and R-LIT-50 states the condition as a judgment recorded against the debtor, while the FSD A2.17.2 step 1 says the trigger is a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer, A2.17.4.4 declares no background event and TSD S4 T5.3 declares no event. The ownership rows of S4 list zero events and zero jobs, so no publisher, no topic subscription and no Temporal Schedule is declared for the step, and the judgment arrives on the rwb-case contract as a stage signal that LitigationWorkflow forwards. The step also runs unattended (FSD A2.17.3.3 primary role None; runs unattended) while the legacy permission table gives the litigation right C to RW-LITOFF and RW-ENFORCE and R to thirty roles, so the story states that the step runs under the service identity with no person right while the two provided operations keep C and R. Neither statement is contradicted, and no event or Schedule is invented.
evidence: Legacy AC1: Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place; When its trigger arrives. FSD S4 A2.17.2 step 1: Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer. FSD S4 A2.17.4.4: None, No background event. TSD S4 T5.3 Events: None. Context pack ownership rows: Events (0), Jobs (0), Workflows (1) LitigationWorkflow. Legacy permission table: Litigation C RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE; Litigation R thirty roles. FSD A2.17.3.3: None; runs unattended, primary; Enforcement owner, also uses.
area: Workflow trigger and access, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the solution architect
proposed: Keep the judgment answer of the rwb-case contract as the trigger of LitigationWorkflow, declare no event, no subscription and no Schedule, and let the P7 rwb-decision owner confirm the decision code of R-LIT-50 and R-LIT-52.

title: The trace result, the trace request elements and the enforcement-decision boundary have no table, no field list and no owning story in the sources
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-017, its Data, Endpoints, Screen and states and Test cases tables); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.17.2, A2.17.3.1 R-LIT-52, A2.17.4.4); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T3.1 legal_action and hearing, T3.2, T4, appendix T-A.2); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (rows R-LIT-50, R-LIT-52, R-LIT-53, R-LIT-54, R-LIT-57); _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows, tables hearing and legal_action)
section: APP s2; s4 Flow steps 8 to 11; s5 X6; s8 BR5 and BR6; s9 State transitions; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.2; s12.7; s12.8; s13; s14; s15; s19; CON s2, s7 AC1, AC2 and AC6, s11, s12.1, s12.2, s12.7, s12.8, s19
description: The trace of R-LIT-52 produces a result the data model has no home for. legal_action carries DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and hearing DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029, and neither carries an asset reference, a trace date, a source or an enforcement decision, no other table of S4 holds the traced assets, and the legacy Data table lists the view and the decision log but no result row. The legacy story's endpoints are the create and read of the legal action, TSD S4 T-A.2 gives LegalActionRequest and LegalActionUpdate with no trace element, and the enforcement decision itself is R-LIT-53 to R-LIT-57 and R-LIT-58, the writ, the deferral and the petition, which are the sibling stories of this service. The case move is answered by this service and applied by the parent CaseWorkflow of rwb-case, which owns recovery_case. Both slices therefore record the result in the local decision record and answer it as a read model, keep the case move as an answer and not a write, mark the trace request and answer element names that no source gives as Not specified in the source documents, and declare the enforcement decision out of scope.
evidence: TSD S4 T3.1 legal_action fields DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and hearing fields DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029 list no asset, trace date, source or enforcement field. Legacy Endpoints: POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions and GET /api/recovery/v1/legal-actions/{legalActionId}. TSD S4 T-A.2 LegalActionRequest, LegalAction, LegalActionUpdate, HearingRequest only. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-52 to ENFORCEMENT_DECISION, R-LIT-53 deferral recommendation, R-LIT-54 writ and seizure, R-LIT-57 write-off referral. Context pack ownership rows: recovery_case not owned, tables hearing and legal_action only.
area: Data model and story boundary, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the business analyst and the data steward
proposed: Fix the trace request and answer element names in the contract review, keep the traced assets in the decision record and the read model with no new column, and confirm in the Dependency Map that the enforcement decision belongs to the writ, deferral and petition stories.
